source.method: sparql:SELECT ?item ?itemLabel ?article ?sitelinks ?discovererLabel WHERE { { SELECT ?item (SAMPLE(?p) AS ?discoverer) WHERE { ?item wdt:P31 wd:Q11344 ; wdt:P61 ?p . ?p wdt:P31 wd:Q5 . } GROUP BY ?item HAVING(COUNT(DISTINCT ?p)=1) } hint:Prior hint:runFirst true . OPTIONAL { ?article schema:about ?item ; schema:isPartOf <https://en.wikipedia.org/> . } ?item wikibase:sitelinks ?sitelinks . SERVICE wikibase:label { bd:serviceParam wikibase:language "en,mul". } } ORDER BY DESC(?sitelinks) LIMIT 160

discoverer.match: Match each element to its discoverer.
discoverer.odd: Three of these elements were discovered by {value}. Which one wasn’t?

rows.label: hydrogen
rows.description: chemical element with symbol H and atomic number 1
rows.hook: is the lightest and most abundant element in the universe, fueling the stars

rows.label: potassium
rows.description: chemical element with symbol K and atomic number 19
rows.hook: is an essential nutrient found in bananas and vital for nerve and muscle function

rows.label: lithium
rows.description: chemical element with symbol Li and atomic number 3
rows.hook: is a soft, light metal used in rechargeable batteries and mood-stabilizing medication

rows.label: nitrogen
rows.description: chemical element, symbol N and atomic number 7; most abundant element in Earth atmosphere
rows.hook: makes up about four-fifths of the air we breathe

rows.label: silicon
rows.description: chemical element with symbol Si and atomic number 14
rows.hook: is the semiconductor at the heart of computer chips and is abundant in sand and rock

rows.label: sodium
rows.description: chemical element with symbol Na and atomic number 11
rows.hook: is a soft, highly reactive metal that combines with chlorine to make table salt

rows.label: cobalt
rows.description: chemical element with symbol Co and atomic number 27
rows.hook: gives glass and ceramics a deep blue color and is used in rechargeable batteries

rows.label: phosphorus
rows.description: chemical element with symbol P and atomic number 15
rows.hook: was first isolated by an alchemist boiling down urine, and is used in matches and fertilizer

rows.label: chlorine
rows.description: chemical element with symbol Cl and atomic number 17
rows.hook: is a greenish gas used to disinfect swimming pools and drinking water

rows.label: actinium
rows.description: chemical element with symbol Ac and atomic number 89
rows.hook: is a rare radioactive metal that glows with a pale blue light in the dark

rows.label: iodine
rows.description: chemical element with symbol I and atomic number 53
rows.hook: is added to table salt to prevent thyroid problems and gives off purple vapor when heated

rows.label: chromium
rows.description: chemical element with symbol Cr and atomic number 24
rows.hook: gives stainless steel its shine and is used for mirror-finish plating on car bumpers

rows.label: manganese
rows.description: chemical element, symbol Mn and atomic number 25
rows.hook: is a hard, brittle metal that is essential for making steel

rows.label: nickel
rows.description: chemical element with symbol Ni and atomic number 28
rows.hook: is a silvery metal used in coins, stainless steel and rechargeable batteries

rows.label: palladium
rows.description: chemical element with symbol Pd and atomic number 46
rows.hook: is a rare silvery-white metal used in car catalytic converters and named after an asteroid

rows.label: iridium
rows.description: chemical element with symbol Ir and atomic number 77
rows.hook: is one of the densest metals, and a layer of it in rock is tied to the asteroid that ended the dinosaurs

rows.label: molybdenum
rows.description: chemical element with symbol Mo and atomic number 42
rows.hook: is a metal added to steel alloys to make them strong and resistant to heat

rows.label: calcium
rows.description: chemical element with symbol Ca and atomic number 20
rows.hook: is the mineral that builds bones and teeth and is found in milk

rows.label: gallium
rows.description: chemical element with symbol Ga and atomic number 31
rows.hook: is a soft metal that melts in your hand, and its existence was predicted before it was found

rows.label: thorium
rows.description: chemical element with symbol Th and atomic number 90
rows.hook: is a weakly radioactive metal named after the Norse god of thunder

rows.label: tantalum
rows.description: chemical element with symbol Ta and atomic number 73
rows.hook: is a corrosion-resistant metal used in tiny capacitors inside phones and computers

rows.label: germanium
rows.description: chemical element with symbol Ge and atomic number 32
rows.hook: is a brittle semiconductor used in early transistors and fiber-optic cables

rows.label: rhodium
rows.description: chemical element with symbol Rh and atomic number 45
rows.hook: is one of the most valuable metals, used in catalytic converters and to coat jewelry

rows.label: francium
rows.description: chemical element with symbol Fr and atomic number 87
rows.hook: is an extremely rare, highly radioactive alkali metal found only in trace amounts in nature

rows.label: niobium
rows.description: chemical element with symbol Nb and atomic number 41
rows.hook: is a metal used in superconducting magnets and jet engine alloys

rows.label: tellurium
rows.description: chemical element with symbol Te and atomic number 52
rows.hook: is a rare, brittle metalloid named for the Earth and used in solar panels

rows.label: neodymium
rows.description: chemical element with symbol Nd and atomic number 60
rows.hook: is a rare-earth metal used in the powerful magnets of headphones and wind turbines

rows.label: scandium
rows.description: chemical element with symbol Sc and atomic number 21
rows.hook: is a light metal used in aluminum alloys for sports gear, and its existence was predicted before it was found
